summary: Seastar Logistics: inflight batch request reordering causing out-of-order completions and SLA breach
description:
Issue summary:
Between 14:00-16:30 UTC on 2026-02-18, Seastar Logistics experienced out-of-order completions for multi-turn sessions affecting ~18% of requests from their high-priority production pool. The behavior caused application-level state mismatch, several automated retries, and an SLA breach for their enterprise contract.

Impact:
- Customer-visible: Incorrect next-step actions in order routing workflows (18% of calls) causing order duplication and manual reconciliation.
- Scope: Traffic for Seastar's priority project across two frontends in us-west-2 (approx 1.2k req/min peak).
- Severity: P0 / Sev1 - customer production outage with SLA exposure.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (prod) serving with dedicated priority routing policy for Seastar (enterprise).
- Model: redwood/gptx-13b-v2 pinned.
- Batcher config: dynamic batching with prefix-aware session affinity enabled.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Send concurrent multi-turn session requests (session-id pinned) with mixing of small and large token budgets to the priority route.
2) Observe that responses for some sessions return with segments swapped between different session IDs under high-concurrency conditions.
3) Replicated in staging once the route policy and batcher config were mirrored.

Logs & telemetry pointers:
- Query logs: link to log stream (redwood-logs/prod/us-west-2/seastar/2026-02-18).
- Traces: trace IDs attached to timeline events in related Confluence page.
- Console dashboard: per-route latency and tail distribution spike at 14:12 UTC.

Why unique/different from other incidents:
This incident is caused by inflight batch reordering tied to a new priority routing optimization that allowed cross-session multiplexing of queued work items when a low-latency slot opened. The result is not standard failover or duplicate completions — it is re-assignment of in-progress batch items between session contexts, which is a rare class of correctness bug for streaming multi-turn users.

2026-02-18T14:05:00Z - Support triages; notified SRE/serving oncall and classified as P0 due to SLA exposure.
2026-02-18T14:12:00Z - Console shows tail-latency spike and increased requeues on priority route.
2026-02-18T14:30:00Z - Mitigation: disabled cross-session multiplexing flag for priority routing and reverted a recent batch-sorting heuristic (hotfix rollout to us-west-2).
2026-02-18T15:05:00Z - Customer confirms reduction in incorrect completions; rate of incidents drops to <0.5%.
2026-02-18T16:00:00Z - Scoped post-incident analysis begins; SRE and runtime teams reproduce locally in staging with reduced configuration.
2026-02-24T10:00:00Z - Patch merged to runtime repo to enforce strict session affinity in the batcher (PR #888).
2026-03-03T08:00:00Z - Patch deployed globally behind feature flag; gradual rollout completed by 2026-03-05.
2026-03-05T12:00:00Z - Final customer follow-up completed; ticket moved to Resolved.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis suspected KV cache prefix collision; however traces showed that requests were being reassigned mid-batch when a preemptive low-latency slot was surfaced by the priority routing optimizer. The batcher had a race in its work-stealing path where queued items lost their session binding. Repro reproduced by artificially creating heterogenous token-length requests and enabling the same optimizer. Root of the bug was a non-atomic update to the batch work queue metadata combined with a new optimization that reorders micro-batches to fill idle GPU slots.
root_cause: A race condition in the batcher + priority routing optimizer allowed in-flight batch work items to be re-bound to different session contexts when a low-latency slot opened. The metadata flip did not preserve session affinity atomically which led to out-of-order completions for multi-turn sessions.
mitigation: Immediate rollback of the batch-sorting heuristic in us-west-2 and disabling cross-session multiplexing for priority routes. Applied additional guard rails to reject rebind attempts when session affinity is present.
resolution_notes: Patch PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/888 enforces atomic session-affinity markers in the batch queue and adds unit and stress tests that simulate preemption and micro-batch reshuffling. Feature flag off by default for priority customers until rollout verification completes. Customer Seastar received a credit covering SLA window and an agreed post-incident action plan.
comments: Support (Aisha): Received customer report at 13:58 UTC. Customer-stated impact: order duplicates and wrong next-step routing. Requested immediate SLO review.
SRE oncall (Miguel): Triage confirmed high-tail latency on priority route and abnormal requeue counts. Started mitigations (disable optimizer) at 14:30 UTC.

Customer (Seastar ops - Priya Reddy): We saw 4% of sessions mis-route in a 20-minute window; our reconciliation scripts flagged duplicates. Thank you for quick response; please advise on exposure and remediation timeline.
Runtime eng (Lena Kim): Reproduced in staging; found race in batcher metadata. Preparing fix and tests. Will open PR and coordinate rollout with SRE.
SRE (Miguel): Hotfix deployed to us-west-2 at 14:45 UTC; customer reports visible improvement by 15:05 UTC. Continuing verification.
Support (Aisha): Sent initial RCA summary and credit offer to customer. They requested a technical walk-through, scheduled on 2026-02-25.
Customer (Priya): Post-fix verification complete on our side. Awaiting final postmortem and timeline for global rollout.
Engineering (Lena): Patch merged 2026-02-24; rollout tracked in INT-4120. Will publish test artifacts and benchmarks.
Support (Aisha): Closing loop with customer and confirming SLA credit processed on 2026-03-05.
follow_up_actions: Add stress tests that mix token lengths and preemption scenarios to batcher CI.
Introduce telemetry that tags batch items with immutable session affinity identifiers for easier tracing.
Create a canary plan for priority-route optimizer features with stricter guardrails and rollout thresholds.
Update runbook to include immediate disablement steps for cross-session multiplexing and communication checklist for enterprise customers.
Schedule a customer-facing technical review with Seastar ops and runtime engineering (completed 2026-02-25).
customer_communication_summary: Acknowledged the issue within 7 minutes of the report. Provided hourly status updates during mitigation. Offered SLA credit for the impacted window and a technical debrief. Customer accepted the credit and requested the follow-up testing artifacts and global rollout timeline.
